name: Business math, binary verdicts
what: Contrarian verdict, the math said out loud, if-A-then-B rules, one fix. Promise, proof, plan.
template: Most [audience] think [belief]. That's why they're stuck.
If [condition A], do [X]. If [condition B], do [Y].
I saw this when [own example, real numbers].
Do that for [time] and the math does the rest.
devices: dichotomies, analogies, value equation (dream outcome x likelihood / time x effort), own numbers as proof, soft or no CTA
compliance: Clinics: never 'free' or discount 'grand slam' offers, no guaranteed outcomes; keep the math non-clinical.
avoid: Borrow structure only: no catchphrases, signature openers, cadence imitation, voice clones or implied endorsement.

name: Blunt evidence myth-buster (physio)
what: Name the myth flatly, why people believe it, what the evidence says, the 'it depends' nuance, simple safe advice.
template: But the research says [finding, cited on screen].
That doesn't mean [overcorrection]; it depends on [factors].
What actually helps most people: [simple, safe action].
Send this to the friend who still [myth behaviour].
devices: rhetorical questions, everyday analogies, humility about evidence limits, research summaries not anecdotes, send/share CTA
compliance: SG health pack: no testimonials/patient stories as proof, no superlatives, no free/discount inducements, no guarantees, sources on stats, label dramatisations; never mock named clinics or competitors; no 'only clinic that'.
avoid: Borrow structure only: no catchphrases, signature openers, cadence imitation, voice clones or implied endorsement.
sources: Lederman 2010 core-stability critique (PubMed 20006294); Lift the Bar podcast; style research Part B #2

Come back and tell me what changed.

compliance: Health: 'can help', never 'this will fix your pain'.
